title: Conjugation criterion for an additive code to be equivalent to a linear code over the quadratic extension field
author: Kanat Abdukhalikov, Duy Ho
work: On the equivalence between additive and linear codes
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 3.1 (source label 'additivecharacterization'), the paper's main equivalence criterion: an additive code over the quadratic extension field, given by a generator matrix G, is equivalent to a linear code over that extension if and only if there are an invertible matrix J over the prime field and a block-diagonal matrix A of two-by-two invertible blocks such that J G equals G conjugated by A against the matrix of multiplication by a primitive element. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete two-directional argument rather than a linear-algebra exercise: it starts from the monomial equivalence between the two generator matrices, uses the closure of the image of the code under multiplication by the primitive element to produce the intertwining matrix J, and then computes the conjugation explicitly by expanding the Kronecker product with the permutation matrix; in the converse direction it constructs the extension-linear code generated by G A and verifies the intertwining relation directly. Turning a code-equivalence question into a conjugation condition inside the Singer cycle is research-level algebraic coding theory, beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
